answers.core: This is core functionality. Godot allows (and encourages) the developer to work with binary data but does not give the full functionality to do so.
answers.workaround:
Not to my awareness. This changes if [PackedByteArray is given full endian settings](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9586), but it is my belief that both are likely to have separate use-cases when the developer is working with binary files. 

One solution would be to create a constant that returns true if the system uses big endian and swap a UTF encoded PackedByteArray back to little endian with a custom method. This would be to avoid edge-cases where the player's machine produces data-corrupting bugs which would ultimately fall on the developer. 

I do not believe that the above solution can be described as "a few lines of script" as it requires the developer to create their own infrastructure that could instead be a core functionality.
